_notes: SGX MiCS-6814 gas sensor (reducing gases e.g. CO, NH3, oxidising gases e.g. NO2) on Pimoroni's breakout at 0x19: a Nuvoton MS51 running Pimoroni's IO Expander firmware reads the three sensing elements with its ADC and switches the heater (as Pimoroni's mics6814 and ioexpander Python libraries do). Detection: the IO Expander chip ID (0xFA-0xFB) 0xE26A - shared by Pimoroni's IO Expander boards; 0x19 is the MICS6814's address. Init: read the pin mode registers P0M1, P0M2, P1M1, P1M2 (0x71-0x74) and ADCCON1 (0xA1); initCode computes read-modify-write values (the same registers set the modes of the pins the firmware itself uses): P0.5-P0.7 input-only for the ADC (AIN4, AIN3, AIN2), P1.5 push-pull for the heater enable; then P1.5 low (bit-addressed P1 write 0x05: heater on) and the ADC enabled. Poll: for each of reducing (AIN2), NH3 (AIN3), oxidising (AIN4): select the channel (AINDIDS0 0xB6), start a conversion (ADCCON0 0xA8 = 0x40 | channel), 2 ms, read ADCRL/ADCRH (12 bits: low nibble of 0x82, high 8 bits in 0x83). Decode: each element's resistance R = raw * 56000 / (4095 - raw) ohms (the board's 56k divider, as the library). The heater needs some minutes to warm up before the resistances settle.
